Letter to ROGER ZELAZNYJ 

_December 1, 1972_ 

## Dear Roger, 

Such a nice letter from you, and congratulations about Devin. Tessa and I have hopes in that direction, but it will be a while before we can be sure. Meanwhile, we are happy for you and Judy. Maybe he will inherit his father’s writing ability. Speaking of writing ability—I dreamed the other night that I was up on a stage making a speech of acceptance for an award, but I was not too clear in my mind what the award was for. Harlan Ellison was the only person in the audi­ ence and he was laughing. I finally was told what the award was for: I had set the Bible into rhymed couplets. I got out of there fast. Fast dissolve. 

...In the beginning God separated the water from the land, And exclaimed, “My, isn’t that grand.” Etc. Which is a distinct loss compared with Martin Luther’s, “And God saw that it good was.” Which I always liked. 

The civilized quality of your letter makes me feel like a barbarian, and my news, which I had promised to tell you, the ravings of a semi-barbaric churl. I arrived in Canada carrying a knife. There’s an example right there, and I got the knife by stealing it from the girl I was going with in San Rafael, whom I ditched, saying I’d be back in California in four days (I’ve never seen her again). In Van­ couver I had an affair with the wife of the reporter who covered the Convention for the _Province._ I also offered to beat him up. I had an affair, too, with a com­ puter programmer who, when I first visited her apartment, asked me two ques­ tions: (one) “Want to smoke dope?” and (two) “Want to go to bed?” I said yes to both. The dope was terrible. On the other hand, I had a really tender relationship with a gentle little hip­ pie chick named Jamis, there in Vancouver, who was the reason for my suicide attempt. I still sort of love her. One day we were on CKLG FM live for almost two hours; the next day I heard her mention to some other people that she was leaving Vancouver in a month.
